items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] I saw a drone suddenly descend towards me. My heart started pounding and I thought, ‘Is this the end of my life?’
items.content_html:
Photographer Zeinab Faraj, 21, found herself buried under rubble beside a dying colleague while reporting in Lebanon. She had never expected to the target of an Israeli missile attack.

It was mid-April and after a month of deadly airstrikes across Lebanon, Israel agreed to a ceasefire. Much of the bombing had focused on southern Lebanon, where entire villages had been demolished. But with the truce, people were hopeful of being able to return to their homes or to see what remained.

Zeinab Faraj, a 21-year-old photojournalist, decided to join Amal Khalil, 42, a newspaper reporter in Lebanon, on a trip to an area in the south of the country to document the aftermath of war. The two had worked together on a number of assignments after Khalil had seen Faraj’s work on social media and contacted her.

items.content_html:
🎨 🔭 ✏️

British Columbia voters are choosing a 93-member legislature Saturday in a snap provincial election called two years early, with the governing New Democratic Party (NDP) and the Conservative Party of B.C. running close in final polls. During the campaign, Premier David Eby acknowledged frustration over the early election call, while both major parties promoted competing plans on affordability, health care and the economy. Eby initially cited U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade threat as a reason to seek a new mandate, then said he should have explained more clearly that the legislature had stalled under the NDP’s narrow majority. Eby also accused interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson of serving as a “Trojan horse” for extremists in his party; Doerkson called that characterization “absurd”. Election officials will count election-day ballots by hand because the snap vote left Elections BC too little time to prepare enough tabulators. Officials will electronically tabulate advance-voting and electoral-office ballots and report those results first. Absentee and mail-in ballots will not be included in election-night totals; they are scheduled for the final count from Nov. 6 to Nov. 10.

items.title: [thehindu.com] Russia and Ukraine agree to Oleshky truce for aid and evacuations
items.content_html: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to pause fighting around Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations under an arrangement brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, officials said Friday. Russia’s military chief and Ukraine’s General Staff said their forces would stop firing at 4 a.m. Moscow time on Oct. 27. The White House had announced Oct. 29 as the ceasefire’s start date, while Ukrainian negotiator Dmytro Lubinets, the country’s human rights ombudsman, said the humanitarian mission would begin on Oct. 29 and the pause would last several days. Oleshky’s population has fallen from about 24,000 before the invasion to an estimated 1,700-2,000, including about 50 children. Residents face shortages of food, medicine and clean water, limited electricity, mined roads and continuing military attacks. The first steps are expected to include assessing residents’ needs and clearing mines before aid convoys enter. Civilian teams are to coordinate transport for those choosing to leave for either Russia or Ukraine. The ceasefire is expected to cover the Kherson region and neighboring areas essential to the operation. Lubinets said it would last several days; officials have not provided details on how compliance will be monitored. Separately, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said technical-level talks involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi.

items.title: [ft.com] Meta posts first free-cash-flow shortfall in at least a decade as AI spending climbs
items.content_html:
🎨 🏔️ ✏️

Meta reported $64.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 26% from a year earlier, but recorded its first quarterly free-cash-flow shortfall in at least a decade as it spent heavily on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. The company also disclosed a new share arrangement for Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg, who had considered leaving California over a proposed billionaire wealth tax. Meta reported $9.9 billion in net income after recording a $9.9 billion charge tied to a settlement with U.S. states over claims involving teen mental health. The company spent about $35 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter and forecast spending as much as $145 billion in 2026. The new nonvoting Class C shares are intended to help Meta raise capital for AI investment and allow Zuckerberg to sell stock without surrendering voting control. He committed to remain in California, or wherever Meta is headquartered, for eight years. California voters decide the proposed wealth tax, Proposition 40, on Nov. 3, and Meta plans to issue the shares in January 2027.

items.title: [reuters.com] Putin agrees in principle to resume Ukraine peace talks after Nov. 10 as Kyiv urges ceasefire
items.content_html:
🎨 🌲 ✏️

Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed in principle to resume U.S.-mediated talks with Ukraine after Nov. 10, following a nearly three-hour meeting on Oct. 21 with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. Kremlin foreign-policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said the technical-level negotiations could take place in Abu Dhabi and focus on a postwar security framework for Russia and Ukraine. Earlier rounds yielded little progress beyond prisoner exchanges. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv supports resuming the talks as soon as possible, preferably by early November, and proposed freezing the current front line as a first step toward a ceasefire. He also called for Ukraine to be included in decisions about its future and said Ukraine’s parliament must approve any peace settlement. Witkoff brought Putin proposals discussed a day earlier with Zelenskyy and European officials in Oslo, including security guarantees and postwar arrangements. Ushakov said the proposals contained little useful material. Moscow continues to seek terms Kyiv rejects, including Russian control of all of Donetsk and a bar on Ukrainian NATO membership. A technical-level meeting is the next step, but no firm date or venue has been announced. The Kremlin said talks could begin after Nov. 10.

items.title: [cbsnews.com] Russia frees detained American Stephen Hubbard during Ukraine peace talks
items.content_html:
🌲 ✏️

Russia released Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American jailed for more than four years, during U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff’s meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday. President Donald Trump said he had personally asked Putin to free Hubbard, who was later flown to Texas. Washington is seeking a negotiated end to Russia’s war against Ukraine. Russia convicted Hubbard in a closed trial in 2024 of serving as a mercenary for Ukraine, an allegation he and his family disputed. The U.S. had designated him wrongfully detained. Trump said no prisoner swap was required, but later argued that his decision to suspend new sanctions helped prevent negotiations for Hubbard’s release from collapsing. Witkoff said the discussions with Putin were constructive. The Kremlin said it was prepared in principle to resume U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks between Nov. 10 and 19, while Putin aide Yuri Ushakov said the latest Ukrainian and European proposals offered little useful material for a settlement.
